sections.heading: Is Capital.com Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Nine years ago Capital.com did not exist. Today it processes $1.27 trillion in quarterly trading volume, holds triple Tier-1 regulation across FCA, CySEC, and ASIC, has secured a MiCA licence in the same cohort as eToro and Revolut, and maintains a Trustpilot rating of 4.8 out of 5 from nearly 2,000 reviews. That trajectory is not normal. Most brokers take two decades to build what Capital.com has built in under one.

The proposition is straightforward: commission-free trading across 5,585+ instruments from a $20 minimum deposit, with no inactivity fee and no withdrawal fees. Spreads start from 0.6 pips on EUR/USD — not the tightest in the market, but competitive when you factor in the complete absence of additional charges. No monthly subscription. No dormancy penalty. No hidden costs.

The AI-driven platform is genuinely innovative rather than marketing fluff. Sentiment analysis, pattern recognition, and behavioural nudges built into the trading interface — tools that actually inform decision-making rather than just decorating a screen. TradingView integration and MT4 provide alternatives for traders who prefer established charting environments.

The concern is straightforward too: nine years is not thirty. OANDA has been running since 1996. IG Markets since 1974. Capital.com since 2016. The regulatory credentials are impeccable. The user satisfaction is exceptional. But the long-term stress-test that only time provides has not yet been completed. If you are comfortable that FCA, CySEC, and ASIC regulation provides sufficient structural protection regardless of broker age — and it objectively does — then Capital.com delivers outstanding value. If you sleep better knowing your broker has survived multiple market crises over decades, the veterans still exist for a reason.

sections.heading: Is Capital.com Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — and the regulatory depth here is exceptional for a broker founded in 2016. Capital Com (UK) Ltd holds FCA licence FRN 793714. Capital Com SV Investments Limited holds CySEC licence 319/17. The Australian entity operates under ASIC oversight. That is triple Tier-1 regulation — the same standard as IG Markets, CMC Markets, and Saxo Bank.

Beyond the Tier-1 trio, Capital.com holds an SCA licence in the UAE and operates an SCB-regulated entity in the Bahamas for international clients. The MiCA licence granted by CySEC places Capital.com in the first wave of brokers fully compliant with the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation — alongside eToro and Revolut.

The FCA entity provides access to FSCS compensation up to GBP 85,000 for eligible UK claimants. The CySEC entity provides ICF protection up to EUR 20,000 for EU/EEA clients. ASIC requires client fund segregation but offers no compensation scheme. The SCB Bahamas entity has no compensation scheme — international clients on this entity have reduced regulatory protection.

Critically: Capital.com has never been placed on the FCA warning list, ASIC banned/cancelled list, or any Tier-1 regulator's enforcement register. The FCA did issue a warning against 'Investing Capitals' operating at investing-capitals.com — this is a clone firm, completely unrelated to Capital.com. The real Capital.com operates at capital.com with FRN 793714 verifiable on the FCA Register.

No enforcement actions. No fines. No fraud allegations. No kill-switch triggered. Clean compliance record since founding in 2016.

NAFT last reviewed Capital.com regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Capital.com Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Capital.com operates a single-tier pricing structure: spread-only, commission-free, same for everyone. There is no tiered account system, no volume-based discounts, no premium account with tighter spreads. Whether you deposit $20 or $200,000, you get the same pricing. This is both a strength and a limitation.

EUR/USD spreads start from 0.6 pips with zero commission — translating to approximately $6 per standard lot round-turn. That is competitive with OANDA Standard ($6), tighter than eToro (typically 1.0 pips / $10 per lot), and comparable to IG Markets' standard offering. Where Capital.com falls behind is against raw-spread ECN brokers — IC Markets and Pepperstone offer 0.0 pips plus $7 commission from deposits as low as $200.

The critical difference: Capital.com charges no inactivity fee, no withdrawal fee, no deposit fee, and no account maintenance fee. When you factor these zero-cost elements into the total cost of trading over 12 months — particularly for less active traders — the effective cost gap versus ECN specialists narrows significantly. A trader who pays 0.6 pips per trade but never loses $10/month to inactivity or $25 per withdrawal is often better off than a trader paying 0.0 pips plus $7 but haemorrhaging fees elsewhere.

Overnight financing (swap) fees apply on leveraged positions held beyond the trading day — this is standard across all CFD brokers and not unique to Capital.com. Guaranteed Stop Loss Orders (GSLOs) are available for a small premium, providing absolute certainty on maximum loss — a feature not all brokers offer.

Leverage is entity-dependent: 1:30 maximum for retail clients under FCA, CySEC, and ASIC rules. Professional clients and international entity clients may access higher leverage.

table.footnote: All spread figures broker-stated. Actual spreads vary by session and liquidity conditions. No inactivity fee. No withdrawal fee. No deposit fee. Overnight financing applies on leveraged positions held beyond the trading day. GSLO premium applies if guaranteed stops are used.

The $20 minimum deposit is among the lowest in the Tier-1 regulated broker space — only a handful of FCA/CySEC/ASIC brokers allow you to start trading with this little.

Withdrawals process in 1-2 business days for most methods (broker-stated). Capital.com charges no withdrawal fee on any method — cards, bank transfers, and e-wallets are all free. This zero-fee withdrawal policy extends across all entities and payment methods, which is genuinely rare. Many competitors charge $5-25 per withdrawal or impose minimum withdrawal amounts.

The payment method range is notably broad: Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank transfer, SEPA, iDEAL, Giropay, Sofort, and various local methods depending on your region. This is significantly wider than OANDA (cards and PayPal only) and comparable to eToro. The inclusion of Apple Pay and Google Pay makes mobile funding seamless.

No minimum withdrawal amount is advertised. Returns go back to the original funding source first (standard anti-money laundering requirement), with profits typically sent via bank transfer.

sections.heading: How to Open a Capital.com Account — Step by Step
sections.body: The onboarding process is clean and modern — reflecting the platform's overall design philosophy. Mobile-first, minimal friction, but thorough on compliance. The $20 minimum deposit means you can test everything without meaningful capital commitment.

The registration form collects personal details, trading experience, and financial suitability information. Takes approximately 5 minutes.

step.text: Upload government-issued photo ID and proof of address. Capital.com uses automated verification — most accounts verified within minutes to hours.

step.name: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
step.text: Deposit $20 or more via card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or bank transfer. Place a small trade, then request a withdrawal to confirm the pipeline works. No fee applies, processing within 1-2 business days.
